text.title: best-practices-2026 Procedure
text.summary: Five-step procedure that scores a repository against the rule set, orders the remediations by blast radius, and locks the result as a baseline in the project's constitution.

step.name: detect-stack
step.action: Identify the pinned TypeScript / React / Next versions and whether Python, ruff and mypy are present and how they are configured.
step.output: Stack manifest feeding the `stack` object of the output contract.

step.name: score-each-rule
step.input: Rule set from `content/01-core-rules.xml` + stack manifest + repository source
step.action: For each rule mark PASS / WARN / FAIL with an evidence path (file and line). Apply the r13-skip-gate first: if it fires, stop here and report the skip reason.
step.reference: Weighted baseline rubric — one item per gating rule.
Report skeleton for the scored result.

step.name: prioritise-remediations
step.action: Order by weight multiplied by blast radius. The strictness flips (r4-ts-strict-flags, r9-ruff-mypy-strict) come first because every later fix is reviewed under them.

step.name: apply-fixes-incrementally
step.action: One rubric item per pull request. Never bundle a strictness flip with a framework upgrade — the combined diff cannot be reviewed, and a regression cannot be attributed.
step.output: PR series, one reviewable change each.

step.name: extract-and-lock-baseline
step.action: Re-score. Extract the project-specific rules into `constitution.md` per r8-snapshot-and-drift, commit the audit report next to it, and record the drift-scan date.
step.output: Baseline locked; `drift_scan_date` set for the quarterly re-run.
